lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Make sure the profile link is a working, professional URL.
Remove the date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They are not needed for most U.S. applications and can invite irrelevant screening.

items.says: Make clear whether the MBA is completed or expected.
items.because: Its current status is unclear.

items.says: Move Harbor Payments above Crestline Logistics.
items.because: The experience section should be in reverse chronological order.

items.says: Excluding weather-delayed shipments does not demonstrate that late deliveries fell.
items.because: It changes the measure and can make the rate look better without improving delivery performance.

items.says: Define the baseline and what the 30% pick-error reduction refers to.
Clarify your role in the slotting changes and who trained the pickers.
items.because: The rollout and training responsibilities are unclear.

items.says: Specify the period or measure behind the forecast-error comparison.
Make the link between the consensus forecast and the error reduction supportable.
Say whether the annual driver hours saved are measured or projected and how they were calculated.
Distinguish your rollout contribution from the tool’s broader impact.
Clarify whether the 35% conversion increase is relative or in percentage points.
Add the timeframe and comparison basis for the conversion result.
Substantiate the claim that the change applied to all merchants.
Do not imply the flow change caused the conversion result without stronger support.
items.because: “After replacing” alone does not establish causation.

items.says: Identify the feature or workstream more clearly and distinguish your contribution from the team’s.
Specify what schedule the two-week early delivery was measured against.
Say whether the work produced a user or business outcome.
State the currency and clarify whether the chargeback-loss figure is an estimate.
Describe the link between your analysis and the roadmap decision more precisely.
items.because: The current wording could overstate how directly your work determined the priority.

items.says: Clarify whether you resolved the tickets yourself or coordinated their resolution.
Add the queue’s starting point or measurement period.
items.because: That would make the reduction by half interpretable.

items.says: Consider whether the ticket-triage detail is relevant to your target roles.
items.because: Product outcomes may be more relevant.

items.says: Explain the opt-in comparison method and its limitations.
items.because: Merchants who opted in may differ from those who did not, so the comparison may not establish causation.

items.says: Combine this measurement detail with the onboarding result or remove it.
items.because: It overlaps with the onboarding-result bullet and may add no distinct evidence.

items.says: Clarify the pilot dates, cohort size, and median calculation.
Avoid presenting the onboarding result as causal unless the evaluation supports it.
items.because: It overlaps with the opt-in comparison.

items.says: Clarify the venture’s status and what your Product Lead role involved.
items.because: The heading may not convey whether this was a live product, student project, or team effort.

items.says: Clarify what the 3,100-student figure counts.
items.because: It could mean students reached, eligible students, or actual users.

items.says: Explain how the 9-tonne figure was measured.
Support the claim that the food would otherwise have been thrown away.
items.because: It is a counterfactual claim.

items.says: Add the measurement periods for active-user growth.
Clarify whether the growth can reasonably be attributed to reminders.
items.because: The interviews explain the rationale for reminders, not their impact by themselves.

items.says: Clarify the baseline and period behind the 95% fill rate.
Explain what “staff cover shifts” means.
items.because: Readers need it to understand the operational benefit.

items.says: Add a substantiated result, recommendation, or decision from the working sessions.
items.because: The bullet describes an activity rather than an outcome.

items.says: Replace the passive, vague description with a clear account of your actions and what changed.
Quantify the form reduction or give another concrete effect, if available.
items.because: Adoption by front-desk staff does not show its scale or benefit.

items.says: Remove the merchant-onboarding bullet from the hospital practicum.
items.because: It is unrelated to the project and duplicates a Harbor Payments achievement.

items.says: Make sure each listed product skill is supported by your experience.
Consider adding directly relevant capabilities missing from the list.
List only tools you have used that are useful for your target roles.
Add relevant tools if you can substantiate them.
items.because: The current list is brief.

items.says: Prioritize the strongest product outcomes for product-role applications.
items.because: Achievements most relevant to the specific job should come first.

items.says: Standardize date styles, punctuation, capitalization, and metric formatting across sections.
Use past tense for completed work and present tense only for ongoing work.
